primitives.name: Remove Horizontal Lines
primitives.verbatim_quote: So we choose to remove many of these horizontal lines.
primitives.assumptions: Lines parallel to the x-axis are discarded because they do not provide meaningful geographic separation between conferences.

primitives.name: Form Two-Conference Split
primitives.verbatim_quote: With each of these remaining lines, we can form two conferences, grouping the cities that are on the same side of the line into the same conference.
primitives.assumptions: Each line acts as a binary classifier that assigns every city to exactly one of two conferences based on its position relative to the line.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degeneracy occurs when a line passes through multiple cities, creating ambiguous assignments that require tie-breaking rules.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Bayesian Network junction nodes in GSI where conditional independence is enforced across conference groups, and to Reinforcement Learning action-value functions in GSE for optimizing conference alignment strategies.

primitives.name: Compute Convex Hulls
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the right of Figure 4 we show the convex hulls of the two conferences that result from using one of the lines.
primitives.assumptions: The convex hull operation captures the outermost geographic extent of each conference, ignoring internal voids or clusters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-convexity arises when a conference contains cities that lie inside the hull formed by others, requiring additional clustering steps.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Support Vector Machine hyperplanes in GSI for maximizing inter-conference margin and to Alpha-Beta pruning search spaces in GSE for eliminating suboptimal conference trees.
layer2.telemetry: Area enclosed by convex hulls serves as a proxy for conference compactness and travel efficiency.

primitives.name: Generate Division Candidates
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each 15-team conference, we can find all lines that split the conference into a 10-team subgroup and a 5-team division.
primitives.assumptions: Recursive binary splitting continues until conference sizes match desired divisional structures, typically 5-team divisions within 15-team conferences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Splitting becomes impossible when a conference cannot be divided into integer-sized subgroups satisfying the required proportions.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Decision Tree partitioning in GSI for recursive feature selection and to Markov Decision Processes in GSE for sequential division formation policies.
layer2.telemetry: Total number of unique division configurations produced per conference measures combinatorial diversity.
